content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text makes an UNDERDETERMINED ruling with stated reasons, so K-S2 governs whether those reasons rest on a single verse's silence or on treating two senses as open.", "verdict": "CLEAN", "quote": "D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.", "room": "The phrase 'a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground' was read either as requiring express reliance on single-verse silence or as covering implicit silence; the judge expressly cites the verse's own words, so neither reading makes it a forbidden ground.", "why": "The judge's stated reason does not rest on a single verse failing to state the link or contrary, and it does not treat a two-sense verse as open; it cites the verse's own words and a footed analogy."}
